system.name: EcoServe
system.one_liner: an LLM-serving system using temporal prefill/decode disaggregation within instances plus rolling activation across instances for commodity GPU clusters

components.name: Scheduler
components.role: routes requests to instances: round robin in NoDG/FuDG, or inter-instance scheduling in PaDG

components.name: Instance
components.role: a serving unit running one LLM Model; in NoDG it colocates prefill and decode, in PaDG it time-multiplexes them

components.role: model weights and KV cache resident on an instance, shown as colored blocks indicating prefill (green) vs decode (blue) work

components.name: Prefill Instance

components.name: Decode Instance
components.role: in FuDG, an instance dedicated solely to the decode phase, receiving KV cache transferred from a prefill instance

flows.what: inter-instance scheduled requests (PaDG); intra-instance scheduling then times prefill vs decode

content.key_idea: Contrasts three placements of LLM prefill/decode work: NoDG colocates both phases per instance (causing interference), FuDG fully separates them onto dedicated instances (requiring KV cache transfer over fast interconnects), and PaDG time-multiplexes both phases within each instance while scheduling across instances to avoid both problems.
content.reading_order: Top row left-to-right: (a) NoDG then (b) FuDG; below, (c) PaDG spans the width, reusing the same Requests-Scheduler-Instance vocabulary and a shared Decode/Prefill legend.

summary: EcoServe targets cost-effective LLM serving on commodity GPU clusters without relying on high-performance interconnects. This figure compares three strategies for placing an LLM's prefill and decode phases across serving instances. (a) NoDG colocates both phases within every instance and round-robins requests across replicated instances, causing prefill-decode interference. (b) FuDG fully separates the phases onto dedicated Prefill and Decode Instances, requiring KV cache transfer between them and thus high-performance interconnects. (c) PaDG, EcoServe's own strategy, keeps both phases on the same instances but disaggregates them along the time dimension via intra-instance scheduling, while an inter-instance scheduler coordinates multiple such instances so at least one is always available for prefill. A shared green/blue legend marks Prefill versus Decode blocks consistently across all three diagrams.
summary_zh: 图比较三种预填充/解码放置策略：(a)NoDG在每个实例内混合两阶段并轮询路由；(b)FuDG将两阶段分离到专用实例并靠KV缓存传输衔接；(c)EcoServe的PaDG在同一实例内按时间维度分离两阶段，并做跨实例调度。
